note: Two-sentence summaries written from each course's own unit titles and topics in role_courses.json. Drafts: a person must read each one against the course page before they are treated as verified. No numbers, prices or ratings are used.

blurbs.PC-AIHR-HRC: A practical introduction to the everyday work of an HR coordinator, from the employee lifecycle and HR policies to onboarding, communications and a capstone project. It is a good first step into HR because it follows the real job, and it ends with a certificate you can show.
blurbs.PC-COURSERA-HRCI: A broad grounding in the five areas HR teams work in: hiring, learning and development, pay and benefits, employee relations, and compliance and risk. It suits you if you want the full picture of HR rather than one corner of it, and it earns a certificate.
blurbs.PC-COURSERA-HRFUND: A short tour of the whole HR cycle, from workforce planning, recruitment and onboarding to performance, retention, compliance and leadership development. It gives you the language to talk about HR work with confidence once you already know the basics.
blurbs.PC-COURSERA-HRPM: Teaches HR from the point of view of a people manager: preparing to manage, hiring and onboarding, handling performance and pay, and finishing with a capstone. It helps you understand the decisions HR supports every day, not just the paperwork.
blurbs.PC-SAP-ECPTO: A short SAP course on how an HR system such as SuccessFactors Employee Central is set up, covering security, employee data and self-service. It is a quick way to get familiar with an HR system, one of the skills this role asks for.
blurbs.PC-GOOGLE-PM: A full beginner programme that follows a project from start to finish: initiating, planning, running it and working in an agile way, ending with a capstone. It is the longest route in, and it leaves you with a certificate and a finished project to point to.
blurbs.PC-UVA-PROJ: A short, plain-language introduction to how projects are planned, how risk is handled and how work gets delivered. It is a light way to see whether project work suits you before you take on the longer courses.
blurbs.PC-EDUCBA-PMSTK: Focuses on planning and scheduling with Microsoft Project and on keeping the people involved in a project informed. It targets two things a project coordinator does daily: keeping a schedule on track and keeping everyone in the loop.
blurbs.PC-MS-PM: A long, thorough programme covering project fundamentals, leading a team, working with stakeholders, agile and hybrid methods, and preparing for the PMP exam. It suits you if you want to go deep and build towards a project management qualification.
blurbs.PC-JIRA: Hands-on practice with Jira: tracking issues, building workflows, planning sprints and running retrospectives. Jira is the kind of tracking tool project roles ask for, so this lets you follow a team's work from the first day.
blurbs.PC-UDEMY-INTROLD: A very short introduction to what learning and development teams do, including how to draft a personal development plan. It gives you the basics quickly, and it assumes you already know how HR works in a large organisation.
blurbs.PC-ILLINOIS-ID: Introduces instructional design, the method for planning and building training, including its tools and the analysis stage. It teaches you how to work out what people need to learn before any training content is made.
blurbs.PC-EDUCBA-LMS: A hands-on introduction to running a learning management system, using Litmos: managing users and courses, reading reports and following good practice. It builds the system skills a learning coordinator uses day to day.
blurbs.PC-SAP-LEARNADMIN: A detailed SAP course on administering SuccessFactors Learning, including items, curricula, programs, classes, assessments and reports. It prepares you to run training administration in an enterprise system, and it is best taken after the platform administration course it lists as a prerequisite.
blurbs.PC-LL-SFINTRO: A short starter in Salesforce that explains what it is and covers the essentials of Sales Cloud. It gives you a first look at CRM software, with no prior Salesforce experience needed.
blurbs.PC-LL-SFADMIN: Prepares you for Salesforce admin work: reports and dashboards, importing and managing data, and everyday admin functions. It moves you from knowing Salesforce exists to being able to look after it.
blurbs.PC-EDUCBA-SFFUND: A step-by-step beginner course on setting up Salesforce, from the interface and fields to user profiles, permissions and sharing rules. It shows how the system is kept organised and secure, which is a big part of an admin's job.
blurbs.PC-SAP-SALES: A short SAP course on the sales cycle in SAP Sales Cloud: leads, opportunities, quotes, activities, forecasting and reports. It helps you see how a CRM follows a customer from first contact to a sale, and basic CRM knowledge will help you.
blurbs.PC-UDEMY-SFADMIN: A quick start to Salesforce administration, from the basics of CRM and cloud computing to building your first custom object and managing security. It is a fast way to get hands-on before you take a longer course.
blurbs.PC-MQ-EXCEL: Takes Excel from the essentials up to advanced across four parts. Excel is a skill this role asks for, so this course turns what you already do in spreadsheets into proven, certified ability.
blurbs.PC-DUKE-XLSQL: Combines Excel analysis, Tableau charts and MySQL databases around real business questions, finishing with a capstone. It teaches you to work with data from start to finish, from asking the question to presenting the answer.
blurbs.PC-MS-SQLPBI: Teaches SQL for pulling data, Excel with Copilot for cleaning and analysing it, and Power BI for turning it into dashboards. It covers SQL, Excel and Power BI in one programme, three skills this role asks for.
blurbs.PC-UCD-TABLEAU: Teaches you to turn data into clear visuals, dashboards and stories with Tableau, ending with a project. It suits you if you are new to Tableau and want to show your data well, not just analyse it.
blurbs.PC-SAP-SAC: A short SAP course on SAP Analytics Cloud: connecting data, building stories, planning and collaborating. It is a quick look at the analytics tool SAP teams use for reports and dashboards.
blurbs.PC-SAP-ERP: A short SAP course on three core business processes in an ERP system: buying (procure-to-pay), making (plan-to-produce) and selling (order-to-cash). It helps you see how an operations team's work flows through a single system.
